_note: Global sim numbers lifted from the prototype. Seconds unless a key says otherwise; distances in logical px.

world._note: Per-world settings (design 14 §9.1 day length, 00 §2 Gentle, 00 §4 Safe, 14 §6 Pets safe, 14 §1 rule 7). dayChoices: the day lengths a world may have, seconds at 1x (night is the last nightFrac of every day). first: a player's first world; later: every world made after it. sim: what the sim uses when a caller gives no settings, i.e. the tools: the prototype's 60 s day, Safe on, no Gentle, no Pets safe, so recorded worlds and the statistical gate stay comparable (14 §9.1).

visit._note: Design 15 §6.1 in spirit, and design 10: somebody new walks in over the hill now and then, so a village that started with two people has somebody to meet. chance: the odds once a day, at first light. minFolk: never before there are this many people already (a first world is not interrupted). Arrivals walk in from the edge, never pop into existence.

bless._note: Design 15 C2: Bless as the life power. meadow: how far the flowers spread when it lands on bare ground, in tiles.

seeds._note: Design 15 C2: what a seed becomes, by the ground it lands on. A list means the world picks one of them. Ground that is not listed grows nothing (rock, path, snow).

storm._note: Design 15 C2: how a thunderstorm picks the tile it strikes. Weights: what is on the tile decides. A lightning rod takes almost every strike and takes it harmlessly; a foil hat is never struck.

dials._note: Design 15 B2 stage 1: four dials (bold, generous, sociable, curious), each low, middle or high. A species baseline lives in creatures.json; the individual shifts at most one step from it, and in stage 1 that step comes from the creature's own id (1 in 6 low, 4 in 6 middle, 1 in 6 high). brave/wander/ooh/share/kin: how far each dial moves the rule it belongs to. crowd: how many of its own kind around a solitary creature count as a crowd.

care._note: Design 15 B3: looking after each other. feedFed/feedHungry: how full a parent must be and how empty the little one, before a meal is passed across (design 15 B3 said 50 for the little one; a baby is only a baby for breed.babySec, about twenty seconds, and starts at breed.babyHunger, so it never passes about 44 while it is still small: measured, and set to 35 so the rule can happen at all); feedPass: how much hunger goes with it. playFull: how fed both of them must be to play, playSec: how long a game lasts, playHeart: seconds between hearts. warnRange: how far an alarm carries to its own kind, and reach: how close is close enough to feed or play.

needs._note2: starveSec: how long an empty belly takes to kill, the same for a mouse and a dragon. starveDps was flat, so a creature died in its own hp in seconds and an owl went in six while a dragon took eighty. desperate: the hunger past which a creature hunts further (ai.huntScanFar) and ranges wider (ai.roamMul), because a meat eater has no food thing in the world at all and otherwise only ever sees as far as ai.huntScan.

mud._note: Design 15 C1: rain turns some of the dirt under it to mud (mudFrac of the dirt tiles, chosen by tile hash so it is the same patches every time), which dries again after drySec. printSec: how long a footprint shows (the renderer draws them; the sim never sees them).

crops._note: Design 15 C1: crops grow through their stages on the terrain timers (terrain.json growsTo and growSec). rainMul: how much faster they grow while it rains. scarecrow: how far a scarecrow keeps birds off, in px.

path._note: Bible 01 §7. Ticks where a key says so; distances in logical px; sepPush in px per second (0.5 px a tick), given on one step in sepEvery (design 14 §7 T2), never to a creature alone in its cell.

save._note: Autosave (design 14 §7 T1, 03 §10): every everyTicks steps (600 = 30 s at 1x), or everySec of real time after a change that is not saved yet (painting while paused, a slow phone), and when the page is hidden.

undo._note: Undo (design 14 §3): how many of the player's steps can be taken back.

hand._note: The Hand tool (design 14 §3): a creature lifted by the player is out of the world (inside = HELD) until dropped. dropAlt: the height a dropped humanoid comes down from, by parachute (the UFO's chuteAlt); hopAlt: the little fall of anything else.

harm._note: Design 14 §6, the harm matrix: what each source of harm may do to a creature, by what protects it. safe: a creature Safe guards (a human while Safe is on; a pet, and later a renamed creature, while Pets safe is on). gentle: a creature Gentle covers (00 §2). neither: no protection. Effects, most protective first: block (the source stops; an attacker shows ? and wanders; a creature that would hunt a guarded one within balkRadius px balks the same way on its think tick), none (no damage; the rest of the event still happens), floor (never below 1 hp), floorFirst (floor in the player's first world, else normal), warn (damage only after warnSec in the hazard, a warning shown meanwhile), normal. null: the column has no say. When both protections apply, the more protective effect wins. The code reads this table (src/sim/harm.js); its fixtures are tools/fixtures.mjs harm-*.

village._note: T13 (design 14 §7 item 13): a village that exists only where the player painted permission. One per world. plan: what it builds, in order, once each; it never restarts, so a thing the player takes away is never rebuilt. maxTiles caps the paint so the site scan is bounded. One job at a time: the village posts a site and one villager takes it.

learn._note: Design: a village works things out from what keeps killing it (Stephen, Sep 20). toFight: villagers lost to something with teeth before they make spears. toSwim: villagers drowned before they make snorkels. weapon/head: what they make.
learn.head: snorkel

flags._note: Design 15: every behaviour change lands behind a switch that defaults ON, so any one of them can be turned off without a rebuild, and so the proof `flag off => the recorded worlds hash as they did` can be run. Turning one off must restore exactly the behaviour that shipped before it.

name._note: Naming (design 14 §7 T11). max: how many characters a name the child gives may keep.

grave._note: Graves (design 14 §7 T11). A grave is an ordinary thing placed where a NAMED creature dies, carrying who it was. max: how many a world keeps, oldest first, so a bad day cannot turn a meadow into a cemetery; 0 turns them off.

react._note: Reactions (design 14 §5). cooldownSec: how long a (row, A, B) pair waits before that row can fire for them again, unless the row says otherwise. maxDepth: how deep one reaction may set off another. tileCap: tile effects in one step, world-wide; the overflow is dropped in file order. placedTiles: how near a new thing must be to another for the placed trigger. coolMax: how many cooldowns are remembered before the spent ones are swept. followSec, tameSec: how long a following or a tamed creature stays that way when a row does not say.

fire._note: Basic fire (design 14 §7 T9): burn, spread, extinguish, regrow. burnSec: how long one tile burns. spread: the chance per second that a burning tile lights one neighbour (rolled on the sim's own stream, so two worlds burn alike). rainOut: how many times faster fire burns down in rain. regrowSec: how long burnt ground takes to come back. dps: damage a second to whoever stands in it (through the harm table as a reaction, 14 §6).
